subject: common octopus
title: Octopuses Tear Open the Crab That's Invading the Mediterranean

scenes.text: An invader is overrunning the Mediterranean, and almost nothing eats it.
Atlantic blue crabs arrived from the Americas and spread with few natural predators.
Then divers in Spain filmed something new: wild octopuses hunting adult blue crabs.
The octopus pins the crab with its arms, wraps it in its web and cracks the shell open.
In tank tests, an adult octopus ate about four hundred grams of crab meat a day.
That's sixteen percent of its own weight. The invader finally has an enemy.

description:
The Atlantic blue crab has spread widely across the Mediterranean with few or no natural predators. In 2025 researchers published the first records of wild common octopuses preying on adult blue crabs, filmed by divers at Calpe, Spain.
In aquarium trials, adult octopuses ate about 415 g of crab soft tissue a day, around 16% of their body weight, leaving the empty shell behind.
Could octopuses keep the blue crab invasion in check?
first_comment: Loggerhead sea turtles were tested too and ate blue crabs whole, shell and all. Who would win: octopus or crab?
